h1: Becoming a brewery project manager for new builds
title: Becoming a Brewery Project Manager | Craft Beer School
desc: What a brewery project manager does on a new build, from scope and vendors to utilities, licences and commissioning. Plus how to prepare for the job.
teaser: A new brewery is a construction project, an engineering project and a licensing project at once. Someone has to hold all three.
standfirst: A brewery project manager brings a new plant from idea to first brew. Here is what the work covers and where people get the skills.
sections:
A project manager turns an agreed plan into a working brewery on time and within budget. The plan might be a 10 hectolitre brewpub or a large packaging expansion. The job is the same: define the scope, schedule the work, manage the suppliers, control the cost and handle the problems.

A new build touches many trades. Civil work, equipment, electrical, plumbing, refrigeration, steam or heating, compressed air, effluent treatment and approvals all need to line up. Delay in one holds up the rest.
The parts of a brewery build

Think of a brewery as five systems the project manager has to connect:

  • Process: brewhouse, fermenters, bright tanks and pipework.
  • Utilities: steam or electric heating, glycol chilling, compressed air, CO2 storage, water treatment and power.
  • Packaging: kegging, bottling or canning, plus labels and pallets.
  • Building: floors that drain, walls that can be cleaned and room for the plant to be serviced.
  • Effluent: brewery wastewater is strong and needs treatment before it leaves the site.

Floors are a good example of a detail that matters. A brewery floor needs slope to drains, a surface that resists caustic and acid and no standing water. A flat floor that looks fine on handover can become a hygiene problem within weeks.

Most overruns begin with a vague scope. Write down what is included: capacity, beer styles, packaging formats, utilities and the services that sit outside the contract. Ask what happens if you want to double capacity later. Leave space and utility headroom for it.

Imported equipment often takes months to build and ship. Installation depends on the site being ready. Work the schedule backwards from your target first brew date and add time for approvals, customs and testing. Our guide to starting a microbrewery in India gives the wider picture of what the owner is trying to achieve.

Keep a risk list. Note the things that could slip, such as a late shipment, a delayed licence or a contractor who falls behind. Review it weekly.

A brewery needs permissions before it can brew and sell. These typically include business registration, building and fire approvals, pollution control consents, excise licences and food safety registration. The exact list and the order differ by state and change over time.

The project manager does not usually write the applications but must know which ones gate the schedule. Work with a licensing adviser, ask them for the sequence and put each approval on the plan with an owner. Do not assume a licence will arrive on the date you hope for.

Commissioning is where the project becomes a brewery. It runs in steps: check the installation against the drawings, pressure-test pipes, run water through every circuit, test the controls, run cleaning cycles and finally make the first brew.

The water trial is a classic. Running water through the system finds leaks, wrong valve positions and pumps that turn the wrong way before a drop of wort is at risk. Then a clean-in-place trial proves that every tank and line can actually be cleaned.

Plan the training too. The team who will run the plant need hands-on time with the vendors before they leave. Keep a snagging list for small faults and close each one with a date.

Project managers come from engineering, construction, equipment supply or operations. Some hold a formal project management qualification, though experience of delivering an installation counts for more.

The strongest candidates also understand the beer. They know why a fermenter needs a cooling jacket, why a lager cellar needs more tank time than an ale cellar and why a drain in the wrong place causes years of annoyance. That knowledge improves decisions on layout and specification. See becoming a brewery operations manager for the person who will inherit your plant.

Sketch the layout of a 10 hectolitre brewpub on one page. Place the brewhouse, fermenters, cold room, stores and cleaning area, then trace the path of grain in and beer out. Count the utilities each area needs. You will find the gaps in your knowledge quickly. That is the point.
faqs: What does a brewery project manager do?
They plan, schedule and coordinate the build of a new brewery or expansion, manage vendors and approvals and lead commissioning to first brew.
Do project managers need brewing knowledge?
They can start without it, but knowing how beer is made improves layout, specification and decisions when problems arise.
What approvals does a new brewery need?
Typically business, building, fire, pollution, excise and food safety approvals. The list and order vary by state and change, so ask a licensing adviser.
How long does a brewery build take?
It depends on size, equipment lead times and approvals. Work backwards from your target first brew date and add time for each approval.
